articles.title: Carlisle United: Nine-man Cumbrians revel in 'incredible' win over Harrogate
articles.summary: Carlisle boss Rob Elliot praises his nine-man side after their "incredible" win over Harrogate.
articles.body:
Carlisle United's task before their game against in-form Harrogate Town - 10 places and 11 points better off than them in the National League - looked a difficult one.

And although the Blues took an early lead against the visitors, who were on a five-game winning run, they then had former Arsenal player Miguel Azeez sent off after just 14 minutes.

Their mission became even more difficult when they were reduced to nine men after 30 minutes when fellow midfielder Harvey Bunker was also shown a straight red card.

It meant Carlisle were two men light with 60 minutes to play against the side sitting second in the National League table.

However, rather than wilt, Rob Elliot's men actually added to their lead immediately after half-time despite being two players down.

They then wrapped up a stunning 3-0 win that will be talked about by the fans at Brunton Park for years to come - but is likely to haunt everyone connected with Harrogate.

Town's manager and co-owner Simon Weaver accused his side of "believing the hype" their winning run had produced.

When asked to sum up his emotions, he told BBC Radio York: "Embarrassed to be honest.

"We came into it with brilliant form but it looked like as a team and a collective we believed the hype coming into the game.

"However, going down to 10 men and then nine men the emphasis was on us to show the required quality on the ball that we have done all season up to this point and we're certainly disappointed and fell well below the standards set so far this season.

"We looked well off it. We didn't handle the situation. Full credit to Carlisle, they deserved to win but we have to look at our performance."

The Sulphurites, who travel to Forest Green on Saturday, are now 10 points off runaway leaders Boreham Wood.

'There was no luck - I'm immensely proud'

Emotions in the other dressing room could hardly have been more contrasting.

"I don't think they appreciate what they've just done," Elliot told BBC Radio Cumbria.

"There was no luck. It was just superb performances and I'm immensely proud.

"I'm hoping it's a catalyst for us to unite and make sure we carry on that momentum. If we can produce this every week then we become a monster and be unstoppable.

"It epitomised what I want from the staff, the players and the club.

"When you are reduced to playing for pure passion, heart, desire and energy it becomes evident of what it means."

The former Newcastle goalkeeper said it was "the most incredible" game of his playing or managerial career and said the players would be given an impromptu day off on Thursday before they play at Altrincham on Saturday.

articles.title: Ivan Toney: Trial for England striker over alleged assault is set for June 2028
articles.summary: England striker Ivan Toney has pleaded not guilty to a charge of assault occasioning bodily harm; trial date has been set for June 2028; nightclub incident occurred in December 2025; Toney appeared in Southwark Crown Court on Thursday and formally entered not guilty plea
articles.body:
The 30-year-old is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6 last year.

Toney appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday morning and formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

During the five-minute hearing, a provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who told the defendant he was "sorry" about the delay.

He said: "That's a long way in advance and I'm sorry about that. As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons."

Toney arrived at court at around 9.10am wearing black sunglasses, grey trousers and a button-up jacket over a shirt and tie.

He was released on unconditional bail after the brief hearing.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men "squared up to each other", before Toney allegedly "lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches".

The criminal case came after a Metropolitan Police investigation and the charge was announced in late July.

Toney represented England at this summer's World Cup and has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League fixtures.

Toney started his career with Northampton and made permanent moves to Newcastle and Peterborough before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

The other Top 25 battle of Week 9 pits the Arizona Wildcats against the Texas Tech Red Raiders in a must-win contest for both sides in the Big 12 title race.

Arizona's emerged as a potential surprise contender in the Big 12, but its only loss is to the BYU Cougars. Saturday's trip to Lubbock will provide the Wildcats with a measuring stick for where it stands.

That's probably bad news for the Florida Gators, who come into Atlanta as an 11.5-point underdog.

Georgia is still one of the best teams in the nation at No. 3 in the AP Top 25. Its also been the dominant side in the rivalry for the last decade with an 8-2 record.

Florida hasn't scored more than 20 points in a loss to UGA since 2007. UGA has 11 wins in a row in which it held the Gators to 20 points or fewer. Florida's scored exactly 20 points in four straight years against UGA, but only one of those defeats was by less than a touchdown.

Georgia started the season with six straight concessions of 20 points or fewer, so it's pretty simple what the goals should be for each team.

If you believe UGA will win, but maybe not cover the 11.5-point spread, you could take the angle of the under on Florida's team total, which is of course set at 20.5.

Florida's been more up-and-down than its rival, as it owns wins over the Ole Miss Rebels and Texas Longhorns, but lost by double digits to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks.

The Gators caught Ole Miss after an emotional win over the LSU Tigers and got to Texas while its offense was sputtering, so there are some reasons to buy into the big point spread.

Georgia is the more proven and consistent quantity with a more experienced quarterback in Gunner Stockton and a defense that doesn't typically break much during a game.

While the spread may be big for a rivalry game, Georgia is more than capable of covering it.

Saturday's clash in Lubbock feels like the first true College Football Playoff elimination game.

Arizona comes in at 6-1 with a loss to BYU already on its resume. It can't afford a second loss against one of the Big 12's three top programs.

A win would set the Wildcats up for a chance to beat Utah at home on November 14 and potentially get into the playoff.

Texas Tech is on thin ice because of its loss to the unranked Cincinnati Bearcats on the road a week ago.

The Red Raiders weren't overly impressive in their first game against a ranked opponent in September. They fell behind by 10 points in the first quarter before they came back and beat the Houston Cougars in what turned out to be a back-and-forth contest.

Texas Tech gave up 458 total yards to Houston and Cincinnati put up 427 yards, including 255 on the ground.

Arizona's offense eclipsed the 30-point mark in each of its victories this season.

All of those numbers give us a good formula for the Over 54.5 to hit.

Neither team has made a convincing argument in their toughest games to trust them on a spread bet, but Texas Tech's defense is leaky enough where points should be scored often.

articles.title: Man Utd crisis: Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good - Gary Neville
articles.summary: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good" as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick.
articles.body:
Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good" as he reflected on Manchester United 's decision to persist with under-pressure Michael Carrick.

United are 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone, following a dismal 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.

Carrick was widely expected to be sacked after that loss, but the club have opted to give the 45-year-old head coach the opportunity to turn things around, and he will remain in charge for United's trip to Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime.

"I reckon what's happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they've literally debated it back and forth," former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast.

"I don't know this, but they've debated it to the point where they've got themselves into a muddle, and thought, 'we'll just stay with him'.

"I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That's when you're really struggling."

Neville added: "Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery."

Carrick's position was precarious even before the Bournemouth game after captain Bruno Fernandes criticised the tactics deployed in the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como last week.

Fernandes was dropped for the Bournemouth match, but he and Carrick have since held talks to clear the air.

"We've all been in football dressing rooms, and they're quite brutal places," Neville said.

"If Bruno Fernandes, the captain of the club... if he comes out and questions the manager's tactics after a 4-1 defeat in Como, where he's played like a drain, and he's been playing like a drain for three months, and the rest of them have as well, that is only 1 or 2% of what they're actually saying internally."

United fans sang Carrick's name as he applauded the crowd after the Bournemouth defeat during what Neville called "effectively a farewell lap".

Those fans then booed the players as soon as Carrick went down the tunnel.

It is understood United's hierarchy have explored the possibility of replacing Carrick, with ex- Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann under consideration.

But, for now, the former Manchester United midfielder is left to bring the group together for Saturday's game at Stamford Bridge, with home fixtures against Roma and Aston Villa to follow before November's international break.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said: "I think he can never say publicly, but I think Michael Carrick would want to be put out of his misery. I really do.

"The thought of going into that training ground now... and trying to do that team talk before Chelsea , when you know the players just aren't having it at all.

"Those players know Michael Carrick's not going to be there in two or three weeks. He knows it, they know it, everybody knows it."

Another former United captain, Roy Keane, added: "He needs the players more than they need him. That's football in a nutshell.

"The players know he's gone, but these are the same players who got him the job last year. So they're running the show."

articles.title: Koundé sigue al margen a dos días del partido contra el Alavés
articles.standfirst: El francés está casi descartado para el sábado
articles.summary: El francés está casi descartado para el sábado
articles.body: Koundé tampoco pudo ejercitarse este jueves junto a sus compañeros en la Ciudad Deportiva, a solo dos días del compromiso contra el Alavés. Salvo giro inesperado, el defensa tampoco estará este sábado a disposición de Hansi Flick para el encuentro en el Spotify Camp Nou. El lateral volvió a trabajar al margen del grupo. Todo apunta a que Koundé se perderá el tercer partido consecutivo desde que se lesionó contra el Betis. El internacional francés terminó el choque en La Cartuja con un esguince de tobillo que le impidió jugar contra el PSG y el Real Madrid. Ahora, todo indica que tampoco estará disponible para el duelo contra el Alavés de este sábado. Además, el cuerpo técnico no es partidario de arriesgar con un jugador que no está al cien por cien, y Koundé todavía no se ha reincorporado al grupo, a falta de solo una sesión de entrenamiento, la de mañana viernes. La más que probable ausencia del francés se suma a las de Eric García, Xavi Espart y Christensen en defensa, así como a la baja de larga duración de Roony. Ante las numerosas ausencias en la retaguardia, Àlex Campos continúa en la dinámica del primer equipo. Este jueves, además, se ha incorporado Guillem Víctor, lateral derecho del Barça Atlètic. articles.title: Beñat San José: "Toda la familia rayista se siente muy orgullosa de lo que hicieron nuestros aficionados"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Rayo Vallecano atendió a los medios de comunicación antes del encuentro ante el Celta de Vigo
articles.summary: El entrenador del Rayo Vallecano atendió a los medios de comunicación antes del encuentro ante el Celta de Vigo
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano recibirá al Celta en su próxima cita. Después de la dura derrota frente al Elche y de la remontada ante el Recreativo de Huelva, el club franjirrojo volverá a Vallecas buscando darle una alegría a su afición. El estadio volverá a estar al 100 % de su capacidad, ya que, después de cumplir la sanción impuesta por la RFEF, reaparecerá el fondo de animación. Beñat San José habló de sus expectativas para el encuentro en la rueda de prensa previa. Accidente ferroviario: "Dar el pésame a todas las familias que perdieron la vida en ese trágico accidente y desear la mejor recuperación a todos los heridos. Todo el país está consternado. Mandar las mejores energías". Rayistas ayudando en el accidente de Urda: "Como entrenador, me sentí muy orgulloso. Lo hemos comentado en el club y toda la familia rayista nos sentimos muy orgullosos de lo que hicieron. Me emocionó bastante y es un gesto que define valores. Agradecer que lo hicieran por todas las personas que necesitaban ayuda. Dice mucho de ellos". Imagen del equipo en los últimos partidos: "El fútbol tiene sus rachas. Estamos trabajando en que no nos metan tantos goles y en acertar más en la definición. Estamos en una racha más incierta y contra el Elche nos pasó de todo en contra". Celta: "Es un equipo creativo que tiene dinámicas ofensivas muy trabajadas. Tiene una fase defensiva muy fuerte. Es muy difícil penetrar esas líneas. Tenemos que mover el balón como lo hacemos, acentuando la profundidad y el acierto en las finalizaciones". Claudio Giráldez: "Es un entrenador fantástico. Es difícil ser profeta en tu tierra y él lo es. El Celta y él están haciendo un trabajo increíble". Bajas para el próximo partido: "Andrei está evolucionando muy bien. Somos optimistas. Los demás, golpes, cansancios, pero ningún problemas más". Afición rayista ante el Recreativo: "Agradezco que fueran a animarnos al partido de Copa. Hubo una química especial. Pienso que la necesitábamos". Partido de Alemao, Kumbulla: "Si trabajan bien y tienen una buena actuación, es positivo para ellos y para el equipo. Alemao es el primero que quiere dar pasos adelante. Trabaja mucho y está siempre presente con una buena actitud. Ha sido muy importante que pudiera meter los goles. Marash un central de experiencia y de garantías que está con buena actitud, con muchas ganas. Veremos si son de la partida, pero están dando pasos para hacerlo". Acercarse al descenso: "La continuidad en el estilo es clave.No creo que nuestra mejora sea renunciar a nuestro estilo. El ser nosotros va por delante. La clasificación está en un puño, no solo se puede mirar hacia atrás, sino para delante. Hay que recordar que tenemos un partido menos y tenemos un margen importante. Haciendo un buen trabajo conseguiremos los resultados". Lanzador de penaltis: "Soy partidario de que tire el que más confianza tiene".

articles.title: La 'prima volta' de Rafa Marín: "Esto es por ti, Diego, que desde donde estés no has dejado de cuidarle"
articles.standfirst: El ex de Alavés, Villarreal y Real Madrid debutó como goleador con el Nápoles... y en Serie A
articles.summary: El ex de Alavés, Villarreal y Real Madrid debutó como goleador con el Nápoles... y en Serie A
articles.body: Rafa Marín (Guadajoz, 2002) ya no es ningún crío... aunque tenga sólo 24 años. Ya ha vivido muchas 'primeras veces': su debut en LaLiga, su estreno en la Serie A, su primer partido en Champions... Le quedan otras tantas, pero en la goleada sobre el Monza (1-4) vivió una 'prima volta' realmente especial. Después de 17 partidos, el ex de Real Madrid, Alavés y Villarreal consiguió estrenarse como goleador, tanto con el Nápoles como en el 'calcio'. Corría el minuto 62 cuando el español se elevó en el primer palo para cabecear un córner botado por Politano y batir a Tornqvist. Lo celebró con rabia, 'partiéndose el pecho' y lanzándose al suelo de rodillas. Había, también, emoción en sus ojos. Por partida doble. "Quiero ofrecer mi más sincero apoyo y fortaleza a todos los familiares y amigos que perdieron a un ser querido en ese tren. Estas cosas no deberían suceder y, sin embargo, ya han ocurrido dos veces en menos de un año. Es una tragedia enorme. Estamos profundamente apenados. Espero, como muchos españoles, que algo así no vuelva a suceder jamás y que se tomen medidas lo antes posible para resolver estos problemas. No hay por qué tener miedo de viajar en tren", había declarado en la previa en 'DAZN'. Su tanto, sin embargo, encerraba una segunda dedicatoria, más personal. Iba para su 'Tito' Diego, que falleció en febrero en un accidente y era un referente fundamental para el central del Nápoles, dentro y fuera del campo, por los valores que le inculcó desde niño: lucha, valentía, humildad, alegría... "Por ti Tito, por haber estado siempre tan orgulloso de él y nunca dejarlo. Te queremos", escribió Yanira Marín, hermana de Rafa. "Esto es por ti, Diego, que desde donde estés no has dejado de cuidarle y darle fuerzas para seguir. Te queremos", posteó Fatima Martín, mujer del central, que no dudó en compartir ambas 'stories' a través de 'Instagram'. "Raf-fica di gol (ráfaga de gol)", escribió la cuenta oficial del Nápoles jugando con su nombre. Un tanto detrás del que hay mucho trabajo y sacrificio. "Para Conte no estaba preparado, ganó el 'Scudetto' con sólo cuatro apariciones, se marchó cedido al Villarreal y ahora es el mejor defensa del Nápoles", desliza 'Sprint e Sport'. "El viento ha cambiado para el defensa español, que nunca se ganó a Antonio Conte y ahora es el centro del proyecto técnico de Allegri", sugiere 'Corriere dello Sport'. Nadie le ha regalado nada... pero puede presumir de ser el segundo jugador que más minutos (963') ha disputado este curso con Allegri. Sólo Di Lorenzo (1.070) le supera. En su cabeza estaba triunfar en Nápoles y lo está consiguiendo, siendo el líder de la defensa junto a Amir Rrahmani. “No ha cambiado nada. En pretemporada, antes de jugar el primer partido ya dije que había mejorado físicamente y, sobre todo, mentalmente. Soy más maduro. Me siento fuerte, también gracias a la confianza del cuerpo técnico y de mis compañeros. Estoy en el 'Napoli', ¿qué más puedo decir? Soy joven, pero es bonito decir que juego con muchos jugadores de primera clase, como De Bruyne y McTominay. Todos. Ellos también me dan confianza, que es importante para un jugador”, reconocía tras el 3-3 contra la Roma. Y es que, a pesar de encajar tres goles, volvió a ser uno de los jugadores más destacados del Nápoles... pero no quiere que la historia se repita. "Estamos trabajando duro para no encajar tantos goles, sobre todo cuando jugamos con un bloque bajo. Es cierto que fueron dos partidos difíciles contra Roma y Bodo/Glimt... pero tenemos que mejorar", reconocía. De fondo en su cabeza, además del Nápoles, hay otra primera vez: debutar con España. Internacional sub 21 en 12 ocasiones junto a Mosquera, Huijsen o Pubill, confía ahora en poder dar el salto a la absoluta. Ya saben lo que dicen en Italia: "Piano piano si va lontano (poco a poco se llega lejos)".

articles.title: Pierre Webo, del ser el 'gol' en Osasuna y Mallorca al banquillo del Dunkerque: el inesperado heredero de Albert Sánchez
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista de Osasuna y Mallorca será el nuevo técnico 'interino' hasta nuevo aviso
articles.summary: El exfutbolista de Osasuna y Mallorca será el nuevo técnico 'interino' hasta nuevo aviso
articles.body: La marcha de Albert Sánchez a la UD Las Palmas ha abierto una nueva etapa en el USL Dunkerque. El club francés ha apostado por una solución interna y ha confiado el equipo a Pierre Achille Webo, hasta ahora segundo entrenador, un nombre muy conocido para los aficionados españoles por su larga trayectoria en LaLiga y por haber protagonizado uno de los episodios más relevantes en la lucha contra el racismo en el fútbol europeo. A sus 45 años, el camerunés asume por primera vez la responsabilidad de dirigir un primer equipo profesional. Lo hace después de acompañar a Sánchez en la aventura francesa iniciada en el verano de 2025 y tras varios años trabajando en cuerpos técnicos en Turquía. Sin embargo, antes de convertirse en entrenador, Webo construyó una sólida carrera como delantero en España. Su desembarco llegó en 2002 procedente de Nacional de Montevideo, aunque inicialmente fue cedido al Leganés. Tras aquella experiencia, encontró su sitio en Osasuna, donde se convirtió en una pieza importante del equipo navarro durante cuatro temporadas. Entre 2003 y 2007 disputó 128 encuentros oficiales y anotó 23 goles, formando parte de una de las etapas más exitosas de la historia reciente del club rojillo. Su rendimiento en Pamplona le abrió las puertas del Mallorca, donde alcanzó algunos de los mejores momentos de su carrera. En Son Moix compartió vestuario con futbolistas como Ariz Aduriz o Juan Arango, consolidándose como un delantero de referencia gracias a su potencia física, capacidad aérea y sacrificio colectivo. Precisamente ese perfil competitivo es el que ahora puede trasladar al banquillo. A diferencia de Sánchez, formado en la escuela del FC Barcelona y con una marcada influencia del juego posicional, Webo representa una figura más ligada al pragmatismo, la intensidad y la gestión del vestuario. El reto será mantener la identidad competitiva de un Dunkerque que aspira a seguir peleando por los puestos altos de la Ligue 2 pese a perder a su entrenador en plena temporada. Pero la figura de Webo trasciende lo deportivo. Su nombre dio la vuelta al mundo el 8 de diciembre de 2020 durante un partido de la Liga de Campeones entre el Paris Saint-Germain y el Istanbul Basaksehir. Entonces formaba parte del cuerpo técnico del conjunto turco y denunció comentarios considerados racistas por parte del cuarto árbitro. La protesta del Basaksehir provocó que ambos equipos abandonaran el terreno de juego y que el encuentro fuese suspendido y reanudado al día siguiente con otro equipo arbitral, una decisión sin precedentes en la máxima competición europea. Años después, el propio Webo describió aquel episodio como un punto de inflexión en la lucha contra el racismo en el fútbol, defendiendo que el suceso demostró que los jugadores podían plantarse ante comportamientos discriminatorios y cambiar la respuesta de las instituciones. Ahora, seis años después de aquel acontecimiento y tras una larga trayectoria repartida entre España, Turquía y Camerún, el exdelantero afronta el desafío más importante de su incipiente carrera como técnico. El hombre que dejó huella en Osasuna y Mallorca, y que acabó siendo protagonista de una noche histórica en la Champions, tiene la misión de dirigir el futuro inmediato del Dunkerque tras la salida de Albert Sánchez

articles.title: NC State outlines vision for football in letter after Dave Doeren's exit
articles.summary: Following the departure of Dave Doeren, N.C. State leaders provided their vision for the Wolfpack football program in a letter.
articles.body:
A day after former N.C. State football coach Dave Doeren said the program's resources must match its expectations, Wolfpack administrators said they're "fully committed" to providing what's necessary to win at the highest level.

In a letter addressed to " Wolfpack Nation" on Oct. 28, signed by N.C. State chancellor Kevin Howell and athletics director Boo Corrigan, those leaders thanked Doeren but said "we believe this is the right time for a new chapter, with fresh leadership and renewed energy to elevate Wolfpack Football to the next level."

Following a 3-4 start, Doeren was fired Oct. 24 in the middle of his 14th season. He leaves as the winningest coach in program history with a 98-74 record, but the Wolfpack hasn't won an ACC championship since 1979 and has only one season (2002) with double-digit wins.

Since the ACC Championship game's inception in 2005, N.C. State has yet to make an appearance while its three Tobacco Road rivals had secured six berths. Duke, Wake Forest and North Carolina have each made two title-game appearances, with the Blue Devils raising the trophy in 2025.

"For this program to become what is wanted and expected, the resources need to match the expectations," Doeren said in his farewell address during a Zoom call on Oct. 27. "That is the reality in college sports. I hope for N.C. State that this commitment to football happens."

Corrigan has been N.C. State's athletics director since 2019 and Howell is a longtime administration who became chancellor in 2025.

"We believe that NC State will compete at an elite level, challenge for ACC Championships, and be positioned for the College Football Playoff year in and year out," the leaders wrote in their letter to fans.

"Together, we are fully committed to providing the financial investment, infrastructure, and NIL support required to compete and win in this new landscape."

The College Football Playoff will expand from 12 teams to 24 teams beginning with the 2027 season, opening up additional opportunities for Power Four programs while putting enhanced pressure on them to reach the postseason tournament.

"We recognize the opportunity, the passion of our fanbase, and the commitment of this University and its supporters," the letter said. "Our responsibility is to translate those strengths into sustained success on the field."

In addition to N.C. State administrators, former N.C. State players Bill Cowher and Dewayne Washington will assist with the national search for the next head coach.

Interim coach Todd Goebbel and the Wolfpack (3-4, 1-3 ACC) will host Cal (3-5, 2-3) on Saturday, Oct. 31, at Carter-Finley Stadium. Kickoff is set for Noon and the game will be televised on ACC Network.

articles.title: Identificado el aficionado que agredió a Camavinga: se expone a una multa de hasta 60.000 euros
articles.standfirst: Los Mossos denuncian al implicado por la Ley del Deporte y el FC Barcelona trasladará el caso a su Comisión de Disciplina
articles.summary: Los Mossos denuncian al implicado por la Ley del Deporte y el FC Barcelona trasladará el caso a su Comisión de Disciplina
articles.body: Los Mossos d'Esquadra han identificado y denunciado administrativamente al aficionado que intentó agredir a Camavinga y a otros jugadores del Real Madrid durante la celebración del segundo gol. El implicado se expone a una multa de hasta 60.000 euros por unos hechos que LALIGA también denunció ante el Comité de Disciplina de la RFEF. La denuncia policial se ha tramitado al amparo de la Ley del Deporte. Si la infracción se califica como grave, la sanción económica oscilaría entre los 3.000 y los 60.000 euros. Esa es la consideración que previsiblemente tendrá el incidente, ya que no se produjeron daños. Si se considerase muy grave, la multa podría situarse entre los 60.001 y los 650.000 euros. A la multa podría sumarse la prohibición de acceder a recintos deportivos durante un periodo de entre seis meses y dos años si la infracción se considera grave. Para las infracciones muy graves, ese veto se amplía a una horquilla de entre dos y cinco años. Los servicios de seguridad del FC Barcelona han colaborado activamente con los Mossos d'Esquadra para identificar al aficionado, que pertenece a uno de los grupos de animación de la Grada 1957. El club trasladará el caso a su Comisión de Disciplina para que adopte las medidas disciplinarias correspondientes.

Week 8 Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Matthew Golden vs. Tetairoa McMillan

When setting your fantasy football lineups for Thursday Night Football, high-end rookie wide receiver decisions often come down to explosive downfield upside versus locked-in alpha volume. This week, we examine an elite stylistic clash at Lambeau Field featuring Green Bay Packers vertical threat Matthew Golden and Carolina Panthers target vacuum Tetairoa McMillan, complete with a deep dive into their respective defensive matchup contexts.

Let's dive into their recent play, fantasy stats, defensive context, and how to approach this Week 8 TNF Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em .

Tetairoa McMillan enters Week 8 sitting comfortably as a locked-and-loaded weekly WR1/WR2 option in fantasy. Through his first several active contests, McMillan has posted dominant numbers on an elite 85 percent offensive snap share. Commanding a massive 26 percent target share, McMillan serves as the ultimate high-floor volume anchor for fantasy football managers.

The Packers boast an aggressive defensive unit, ranked inside the top 10 in limiting opposing wide receiver efficiency and keeping plays in front of them. Going on the road to Lambeau Field on a short week presents a tough environment for the Panthers' passing game. However, McMillan's alpha role and heavy target volume insulate him from tough matchups because Carolina is forced to lean on him early and often to move the chains. Even against a stout Green Bay defense, his double-digit target expectation keeps his floor safe.

Matthew Golden enters Week 8 continuing to function as one of the most explosive vertical elements in the Green Bay passing attack. Across seven games this season, Golden has hauled in 36 receptions for 540 yards and 3 touchdowns on 69 targets, averaging a stellar 16.8 PPR fantasy points per game. Boasting massive downfield equity, highlighted by a top-10 air-yards share and heavy red-zone involvement, Golden's projected weekly ceiling remains sky-high.

The Panthers' secondary has experienced heavy leakage against perimeter wide receivers, surrendering chunk plays and ranking in the lower third of the NFL in explosive pass plays allowed over 20 yards. While Carolina struggles to lock down vertical boundary receivers (which plays directly into Golden's skill set as a deep-threat burner), the Packers' offense, as a home favorite, may lean heavily on the ground game if they control the game script. Golden's reliance on high-efficiency, lower-volume deep conversions creates a weekly floor that can fluctuate if the big plays do not materialize.

While Matthew Golden benefits from an enticing matchup against a vulnerable Carolina secondary that gives up big vertical plays, his weekly volatility makes him a bit more boom-or-bust. Tetairoa McMillan's unmatched target security and alpha-role status make a tough road matchup against Green Bay's defense manageable. We have McMillan ranked a bit higher in our Week 8 Wide Receiver Rankings . Fire up McMillan for guaranteed volume and high-end PPR reliability, while treating Golden as a high-upside WR2.

Leeds have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season.

Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues.

Leeds' defensive line once again delivered FPL managers solid returns with our showing in Gameweek 8. James Trafford (£5.0m) topped the pile among his colleagues, collecting 10 points for his clean sheet, a save point, the maximum of three bonus points, and his two appearance points for completing 90 minutes. Trafford has earned save points in all but one of his games this campaign, and has two double-digit returns to his name.

Following his assist in Gameweek 7, Tarik Muharemović (£5.1m) scored nine points last time out against Sunderland, with his clean sheet, one bonus point, two Defensive Contribution points and two appearance points. Defenders are awarded two extra points in FPL if they complete 10 or more defensive actions (clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles won) in a single game.

Jaka Bijol (£5.0m) also picked up Defensive Contribution returns and finished on eight points for the game, while Gabriel Gudmundsson (£4.5m) and James Justin (£4.5m) finished with six points apiece.

Player Spotlight: Tarik Muharemović (£5.1m)

Muharemović is becoming a real force in FPL. Over the course of the season so far, he has returned in every single game, with the exception of Gameweek 6. It is the kind of consistency that FPL managers love to have in their teams and will surely lead to an increase on his current 5.6 per cent ownership across the game.

What makes the Bosnian international such an exciting prospect in FPL is the many areas in which he collects points. The centre-half has two assists in eight league games, which is the joint-most in the Leeds squad this season, while his six headed goal attempts from set plays is a team high, and suggests he could find himself on the scoresheet in the near future.

At the other end of the pitch, Muharemović has hit the threshold for Defensive Contribution points in five of the eight games to date, earning himself 10 extra points across the season for defensive actions alone. With a total of 43 points, Tarik is Leeds' second-highest scorer in the game right now and it wouldn't be a surprise to see him competing for top spot among his team-mates come the end of the season.

Arsenal's Gabriel (£7.9m) was the highest scorer of Gameweek 8, registering 17-points. He scored a goal, picked up a clean sheet, hit the defensive contribution threshold and was awarded three bonus points in his side's win against Everton.

His defensive colleague Ezri Konsa (£4.7m) also scored well. He earned himself 14-points due to his goal, a clean sheet and finishing just behind Gabriel on two bonus points. Completing the top three was Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson (£6.7m). He netted twice against Manchester City and was awarded three bonus points, finishing the game with 13 points. He is also the most transferred in player ahead of Gameweek 9 at the time of writing.

articles.title: Neville warns managers can need sacking 'for their own good' as Carrick fights on
articles.summary: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed "for their own good" as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick.Neville, a...
articles.body:
Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed "for their own good" as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick.

Carrick's future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win.

Sunday's 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

But former United and England midfielder Carrick, 45, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match press conference later Thursday ahead of the team's league match away to Chelsea on Saturday.

"I reckon what's happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they (the United hierarchy) literally debated it (Carrick's future) back and forth," former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast.

"I don't know this, but they've debated it to the point where they've got themselves into a muddle, and thought, 'we'll just stay with him'.

"I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That's when you're really struggling."

Neville, a former United team-mate of Carrick, added: "Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery."

Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford.

Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth.

Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United's current malaise.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team's struggles under Ruben Amorim -- United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

Neville believes the root of United's woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying "enough is enough" as he urged them to sell-up.

The Glazers took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005. They remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to British billionaire businessman Jim Ratcliffe in 2024 .

Neville, a longstanding critic, reiterated his call for the US-based family to sell.

"There's £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they're hamstrung in some ways," said Neville, adding: "You've got a failure of 13, 14 years on the football side, you've subbed it out to somebody else (Ratcliffe), which is ridiculous, and not took responsibility...Enough is enough, they have to sell the whole the club. The fans have had enough. They have to go now."

articles.title: Premier League: Why is there no fixture on Sunday at 2pm?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains where is no 14:00 GMT kick-off on Sunday in the Premier League this weekend.
articles.body:
Unlike many Premier League weekends this season, there will be no 14:00 GMT kick-off this Sunday.

The time slot is one of the most frequently used in a typical Premier League weekend programme.

There is usually at least one match at 14:00 each Sunday - and this season there have at times been more, which is a knock-on effect of four Premier League clubs competing in the Europa League and Conference League on a Thursday evening. Teams usually want at least two clear days between games.

Last weekend, four matches were played early on Sunday, and only two fixtures kicked off in the traditional Saturday 15:00 slot.

In contrast, this weekend will feature five games at 15:00 on Saturday, and only one on Sunday - Liverpool taking on Arsenal at 16:30.

There will also be kick-offs at 12:30, 17:30 and 20:00 on Saturday, and finally at 20:00 on Monday.

The absence of an early Sunday game is because of Aston Villa's involvement in this season's Champions League.

Villa's meeting with Fulham at Villa Park was the designated 14:00 match for Sunday afternoon.

But because Unai Emery's Villa side have a Champions League match at Barcelona two days later - on Tuesday, 3 November - the Fulham game has been brought forward to 20:00 on Saturday.

As Sky Sports was due to show the match in its initial slot, the broadcaster will also show the rearranged game.

articles.title: Flick abre la puerta a fichar un central en el mercado invernal
articles.standfirst: La decisión no está tomada porque depende de muchos factores
articles.summary: La decisión no está tomada porque depende de muchos factores
articles.body: El FC Barcelona vuelve a tener sobre la mesa la posibilidad de reforzar el eje de la defensa en el próximo mercado de invierno. Aunque la operación todavía no está decidida y depende de varios factores deportivos y económicos, Hansi Flick estaría ahora abierto a incorporar un central si las circunstancias lo permiten. Una opción que el club ya valoró durante el pasado verano, pero que acabó descartándose por decisión del técnico alemán. En la planificación de la anterior ventana de fichajes, la dirección deportiva azulgrana contempló la llegada de un defensa central para apuntalar una posición especialmente importante en el esquema de Flick. Entre los nombres que más sonaron estuvo el de Alessandro Bastoni, uno de los pilares del Inter de Milán. Sin embargo, pese a las conversaciones y los rumores que rodearon la operación, el entrenador consideró finalmente que no era necesario realizar una incorporación para esa demarcación. La situación, no obstante, ha cambiado. El rendimiento de la línea defensiva no está ofreciendo todas las garantías esperadas, en una dinámica que recuerda a algunos de los problemas que el equipo ya sufrió la temporada pasada. A ello se suma el elevado número de lesiones que está condicionando la planificación del técnico y reduciendo sus alternativas para configurar una defensa fiable y competitiva. En este contexto, la posibilidad de acudir al mercado vuelve a ganar fuerza después de las últimas conversaciones del técnico y la Dirección Deportiva. La disponibilidad de Andreas Christensen es también un factor que invita a la prudencia a la hora de planificar la temporada, ya que el Barça no puede contar con él con todas las garantías. La acumulación de contratiempos físicos hace que el club deba valorar si dispone con él de suficientes efectivos para afrontar con seguridad la segunda parte del curso. El danés lleva más de un mes lesionado. La decisión, sin embargo, no será sencilla. El mercado de invierno suele ofrecer menos oportunidades que el de verano, puesto que muchos clubes no están dispuestos a desprenderse de sus jugadores a mitad de temporada. Por ello, si el Barcelona acaba dando el paso, tendrá que estudiar con detenimiento qué perfil encaja mejor en sus necesidades: un defensa contrastado, con experiencia al máximo nivel y capacidad para ofrecer un rendimiento inmediato, o un central más joven, con proyección y margen de crecimiento para convertirse en una apuesta de futuro. La viabilidad económica será otro elemento determinante. El margen de 'Fair Play' financiero del que disponga el club condicionará tanto la operación como el tipo de futbolista al que pueda aspirar. En los despachos deberán analizar las posibilidades reales de incorporar un refuerzo. En ese escenario, también habrá que seguir de cerca la situación de Alejandro Balde. El lateral podría plantearse una salida si continúa teniendo menos minutos de los esperados. Una eventual marcha permitiría al Barça liberar espacio dentro de su planificación de plantilla y podría facilitar la llegada de un nuevo jugador, siempre en función de las condiciones económicas de la operación. Por ahora, el fichaje de un central no pasa de ser una posibilidad que el Barcelona mantiene abierta. Flick, que en verano prefirió no reforzar esa posición, está dispuesto a reconsiderar su postura ante las necesidades actuales del equipo. La decisión final dependerá de las oportunidades que ofrezca el mercado, del estado físico de la plantilla y de la capacidad económica del club. El Barça tiene el debate abierto.

articles.title: Monchi defiende el despido de Manolo: "Educación tengo, y mucha"
articles.standfirst: El director general deportivo del Espanyol asume su responsabilidad en la crisis, explica por qué comunicó el cese en el vestuario y apuesta por Sarabia para lograr la permanencia y construir una identidad
articles.summary: El director general deportivo del Espanyol asume su responsabilidad en la crisis, explica por qué comunicó el cese en el vestuario y apuesta por Sarabia para lograr la permanencia y construir una identidad
articles.body: Monchi dio la cara para explicar el cambio de rumbo en el banquillo del Espanyol. Con Manolo González destituido y Eder Sarabia como nuevo entrenador hasta junio de 2028, el director general deportivo defendió tanto la decisión como la manera de comunicarla, asumió su parte de responsabilidad en la situación del equipo y lanzó un mensaje a la plantilla: el relevo en el banquillo también exige una reacción de los futbolistas. La cuestión más delicada de su comparecencia estuvo en las formas del adiós a Manolo. Monchi rechazó las críticas sobre el trato dispensado al técnico y explicó que la conversación se produjo en el vestuario, después del partido contra el Sestao. "He leído y escuchado que la destitución de Manolo fue de poca educación y ya digo yo que educación tengo mucha", afirmó. El dirigente sostuvo que retrasar la comunicación hasta el regreso a Barcelona habría generado una situación todavía más incómoda. Compartir el autobús y el avión con el entrenador, hablar del siguiente encuentro y anunciarle después su salida no le parecía una alternativa más respetuosa. "Habría sido reírme de él sentarme a su lado en el avión y no decirle nada sobre su futuro", argumentó. Según su explicación, el cese se trasladó en una conversación afectuosa y desde el dolor de tener que despedir a un compañero. "La destitución está hecha desde el máximo respeto, creyendo que era el momento. La varita del momento no la tenemos", señaló. También desveló que Manolo tuvo la posibilidad de comparecer junto a él para despedirse y ofrecer sus explicaciones, pero rechazó la invitación. El agradecimiento al técnico gallego acompañó a la defensa de una decisión marcada por los resultados. Monchi aseguró que había confiado en su continuidad y que no se arrepentía de haber apostado por él en mayo. La acumulación de encuentros sin ganar terminó por agotar esa vía. La determinación definitiva, precisó, llegó después del encuentro de Sestao. "Me siento culpable" Monchi evitó situar toda la responsabilidad en el entrenador saliente. Reconoció que prescindir de un técnico supone también un fracaso para quien lo ha respaldado y extendió la autocrítica al resto del club. "Me siento culpable de la situación actual. Todos, y yo el primero, hemos de dar más. Los jugadores también", manifestó. El director general deportivo reclamó a los futbolistas que revisen su rendimiento y asuman su responsabilidad: "Han de darse cuenta de que la cuerda se rompe por el lado más fácil, pero ellos también tienen culpa". Tampoco separó a los fichajes del resto del vestuario. A su juicio, el rendimiento de las incorporaciones ha seguido la misma línea que el del equipo, sin suficientes respuestas individuales que permitan cambiar la dinámica. Recuperar la confianza y elevar la exigencia forman parte del trabajo inmediato. Sarabia, una apuesta más allá de la urgencia La llegada de Eder Sarabia responde a una doble intención. La primera es sacar al Espanyol de la zona de descenso. La segunda, construir un equipo con un estilo reconocible. "No solo quería un entrenador que salve al Espanyol, también que le dé una identidad, filosofía e idea de juego", explicó Monchi. El dirigente considera que la plantilla dispone de futbolistas adecuados para la propuesta del nuevo entrenador, basada en el protagonismo con balón. Aunque admitió que implantar ese modelo requiere tiempo, defendió que existe margen para corregir el rumbo: "Estamos en una situación difícil, no estamos desahuciados ni mucho menos". La prioridad será adaptar esa idea a la urgencia competitiva. El parón permitirá avanzar en el trabajo, pero los primeros partidos obligarán a concretar las propuestas. Monchi, que prefirió aplazar el debate sobre el mercado de invierno, insistió en su confianza en los recursos actuales. Sarabia ya está inscrito como entrenador del Espanyol, aunque la sanción que arrastra retrasará su estreno en el banquillo hasta el encuentro ante el Athletic en Bilbao. Sergio García dirigirá al equipo frente al Villarreal. Monchi agradeció su disposición y valoró su trabajo en el filial, aunque consideró que entregarle ahora el primer equipo habría supuesto precipitar etapas. Al nuevo técnico le espera una tarea que empieza por la clasificación. "Primero hay que apagar un fuego", resumió Monchi. Después llegará el momento de dar forma al Espanyol que pretende construir.

articles.title: Maresca braced for another tough test in Brighton repeat
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has warned his side to expect no let-up from Brighton this weekend when the teams meet again just days after a dramatic...
articles.body:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has warned his side to expect no let-up from Brighton this weekend when the teams meet again just days after a dramatic cup tie.

League Cup-holders City edged the Seagulls on penalties to reach the quarter-finals on Wednesday after twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 at the Etihad Stadium.

After making 16 changes between them, both Maresca and Brighton counterpart Fabian Hurzeler are set to revert to their full-strength sides when the teams meet in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday.

Table-toppers City are level on points with champions Arsenal, while third-placed Brighton are just five points behind the leading duo.

"They (Brighton) are in a brilliant moment," said Maresca. "They are winning games, they are scoring goals. They are scoring many goals every game –- three, four, five, goals a game.

"I've watched all their Premier League games since we started, and since the first day –- against Arsenal, (Crystal) Palace, Liverpool, they always go front foot, man to man.

"We knew that this was a tough game and they're going to be exactly the same on Saturday," added Maresca.

Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter's shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards.

Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards.

Rutter restored Brighton's lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam's cut-back.

Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki's 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City.

Kovacic's penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton's Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.

City's season continues under the shadow of being found guilty last month on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict.

No punishment has yet been announced, however, and Maresca -- who has repeatedly stated his complete trust in City's hierarchy -- remains focused on on-field issues, with his side drawn at home to third-tier Bradford in the League Cup quarter-finals.

"It's a different competition but the ambition has to be the same," said Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola after the Spaniard stepped down at the end of last season following a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad.

"This is a new project with new players, a new manager. It started three months ago.

"We need to do our business. That is winning games and, at the moment, we are doing that."

Brighton will remain in the northwest between the two games rather than travelling back to the south coast.

"Having two away games and not sleeping in your own bed, you can't see it as an advantage but we will try to make the best of it," said Hurzeler. "We will not try to find any excuses.

He added: "We'll come back with full energy, full enthusiasm and we go on Saturday."

articles.title: Arsenal are one of the clubs considering move for Serie A wonderkid
articles.summary: Nico Paz transfer latest as Como block January move amid Chelsea and Arsenal interestComo have made their position clear on Nico Paz, with TeamTalk reporting...
articles.body:
Nico Paz transfer latest as Como block January move amid Chelsea and Arsenal interest

Como have made their position clear on Nico Paz, with TeamTalk reporting that the Serie A club have no intention of sanctioning a January sale despite mounting interest from Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester United. For now, the message from Italy is firm, and it centres on one of Europe's fastest-rising attacking midfielders.

The 22-year-old has become a key figure in Cesc Fàbregas's plans since arriving from Real Madrid in 2024. After a 2025/26 campaign that delivered 13 goals and eight assists in all competitions, Como moved to make the deal permanent for €60million, which is £50.3m. That outlay already looks justified.

Paz's recent Champions League performance against Manchester United, when he registered two goals and an assist, has only intensified the spotlight. Chelsea have tracked him closely, while Arsenal and United are also credited with strong interest. TeamTalk states that "Como have no intention of selling Nico Paz in January" and that view appears to be shared throughout the club.

Internally, Paz is regarded as central to the project. As TeamTalk explains, "Como view Paz as indispensable to their ambitions, particularly as they compete in the Champions League for the first time in their history." That line gives useful context to their refusal to entertain winter approaches.

The report adds that "Club sources have repeatedly emphasised that the player is not for sale in the short term," with Fàbregas also valuing stability in his attacking structure. Paz has settled well, developed quickly and, crucially, appears happy with the responsibility being placed on him in Italy.

There are further layers to this situation. Chelsea's admiration is long-standing and Arsenal's interest is noted, but Real Madrid still hold significant leverage through a buy-back clause worth €80million, which is £67.1m, active in the summer of 2027. TeamTalk also notes that "Sources have even suggested Como could demand €100million-plus from outside suitors," which would place any deal well into premium territory, at least £83.9m.

That contractual protection strengthens Como's hand and makes a January breakthrough highly unlikely. "Until then, Como are expected to hold firm and protect one of their most valuable assets." In practical terms, this feels like a story that will build towards the summer rather than one resolved in the next window.

For full credit, the original report comes via TeamTalk. Their summary of Como's position is blunt and definitive: "there is no way they will sell the star in January, hands off."

Summer transfer window may define next step

If Paz maintains this level through the second half of the season, interest will only intensify. His value could rise further, his profile could broaden again and the queue of elite clubs may lengthen. At present, though, Como are protecting an asset they see as vital, and every indication is that Arsenal, Chelsea and others will need patience.

This is exactly the kind of update that invites excitement, even if the short-term outlook sounds closed. A player producing those numbers, thriving in the Champions League and being described as indispensable to his club is naturally going to catch the eye. The attraction is obvious. Paz sounds like the sort of attacking midfielder who can shift a match with one clever pass, one sharp movement, or one decisive finish.

What stands out most is the timing. January always felt difficult once Como made him permanent and built so much around him. If they are in the Champions League and treating him as a cornerstone, there was never much reason for them to weaken mid-season. That part rings true.

The more intriguing angle is whether the summer becomes a genuine opening. If the price climbs towards €100million, which is £83.9m, then any move becomes a major strategic decision rather than an opportunistic signing. Arsenal would need to be completely convinced that Paz is not only talented, but the right fit for the structure, the pressing demands and the creative burden in big matches.

There is also the Real Madrid element hanging over everything. A buy-back clause always changes the mood of a chase because it can leave other clubs doing the groundwork only for Madrid to step in at the perfect moment. Even so, this is one to watch closely. If an elite creator with upward momentum becomes available, it is hard not to be interested.

articles.title: El Tourmalet del Almería arranca en Ipurua
articles.standfirst: Una sola victoria rojiblanca en ocho visitas al feudo del Eibar, la última en la temporada 2005/06, y tras ello llegará Montilivi
articles.summary: Una sola victoria rojiblanca en ocho visitas al feudo del Eibar, la última en la temporada 2005/06, y tras ello llegará Montilivi
articles.body: Superado el susto copero ante el Castellonense y con el billete para la siguiente ronda sellado tras una agónica remontada, la UD Almería vuelve a centrar todos sus esfuerzos en la Liga. Y lo hace con un calendario que pondrá a prueba sus aspiraciones en apenas una semana. El primer examen llegará este sábado en Ipurua, donde los de García Pimienta defenderán la segunda plaza frente a un Eibar que les sigue de cerca, a solo tres puntos de distancia. El conjunto armero se ha consolidado como uno de los grandes candidatos al ascenso y una victoria le permitiría igualar a los rojiblancos en la clasificación. El Almería afronta, por tanto, un duelo de máxima exigencia en uno de los escenarios más complicados de la categoría y, además, históricamente maldito para los indálicos. Los rojiblancos no ganan en Ipurua desde la temporada 2005/06 y han salido derrotados en cada una de sus siete últimas visitas. Como si fuera poco, apenas habrá margen para el descanso, ya que la siguiente jornada deparará otro enfrentamiento directo, esta vez en Montilivi frente al Girona. El conjunto catalán es cuarto, se encuentra a cuatro puntos del Almería y atraviesa uno de sus mejores momentos del curso, con seis jornadas consecutivas sin conocer la derrota. Dos compromisos seguidos ante rivales de la zona alta que pueden marcar el rumbo del conjunto almeriense antes del tramo final de la primera vuelta. El equipo de García Pimienta llega bien posicionado en la clasificación, pero es consciente de que este exigente calendario puede reforzar su candidatura al ascenso o comprimir todavía más una pelea que se presenta apasionante. Tras el aviso recibido en la Copa del Rey y el doloroso empate cedido ante el Oviedo en Liga, el margen de error vuelve a estrecharse y el verdadero Tourmalet de los rojiblancos comienza ahora. Eso sí, el Almería afronta este desafío avalado por una racha de nueve partidos consecutivos sin perder entre Liga y Copa, además de haber saldado con victoria sus tres últimas salidas.
